PullRequest.Title: Preserve sandbox history when live hydration fails
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Follow-up to #340354, addressing [the live-hydration review finding](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340354#discussion_r4227139850). No separate tracking issue was supplied.

`AgentHostSessionHandler` can fulfill its content request with an error transcript or an empty root-session fallback after a subscription failure. The sandbox facade previously treated either result as a successful live snapshot, replacing recorded messages, invalidating their cache, cancelling the recorded refresh, and disabling its recovery paths.

- Expose an optional, explicit initial-history failure outcome rather than inferring failure from empty history or historical error responses. Other consumers keep their existing error rendering.
- Reject failed live promotion while retaining the recorded transcript, cache, ongoing history refresh, and existing live Retry action. Release the rejected session and its subscriptions, including failures before a chat URI was resolved.
- Preserve genuinely new sessions, successfully hydrated empty chats, and conversations containing failed historical turns. A missing root session can still initialize lazily, but only after the already-running recorded read successfully confirms there is no conversation to preserve.
- A truncated replay that omits the requested root reports incomplete history, not an empty conversation. Partial transcripts containing the requested root remain readable with their existing warning.

No new setting, protocol field, storage key, telemetry event, or banner is introduced. Recorded-history recovery still does not reconnect or submit input.

## Validation

Truncated-root follow-up (`d9b11a29af2`), using Node 24.18.0:

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — **passed**.
- `node build/hygiene.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxReadOnlySessionHandler.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxReadOnlySessionHandler.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `git diff --check` — **passed**.
- The following selection **passed 86 tests**, including both new missing-root truncation regressions and the existing readable-partial-history case. Both new cases failed before the one-line validation fix.

```sh
xvfb-run -a ./scripts/test.sh --no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxSessionHandler.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxHistoryCache.test.ts \
  --grep 'history loading cloud sandbox promotion|CloudSandboxSessionHandler|CloudSandboxHistoryCache'
```

Initial fix (`e5ac639c4b8`), using Node 24.18.0:

- `npm run install-fast` — **passed** after the new main branch's SDK/runtime version check identified stale dependencies. No dependency manifests changed.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — **passed**.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — **passed**, including the final cancellation/subscription-release assertions.
- `node build/hygiene.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatSessionsService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxSessionHandler.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` — **passed**. After adding cancellation/subscription-release coverage, `node build/hygiene.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` also **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatSessionsService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxSessionHandler.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` — **passed**, all four changed files.
- `git diff --check` — **passed**.

The following focused selection **passed 130 tests**, including 12 real-provider sandbox promotion cases:

```sh
xvfb-run -a ./scripts/test.sh --no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxSessionHandler.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxHistoryCache.test.ts \
  --grep 'history loading|history with tool events|disposal|does not render a load failure|still renders a load failure|CloudSandboxSessionHandler|CloudSandboxHistoryCache'
```

The real-provider regression cases reproduced eight failures on the unfixed implementation, including cache invalidation, transcript replacement, cancelled recorded reads, and lost retry. One intermediate Electron launch crashed during module loading (exit code 5), before executing tests; the final identical selection completed successfully.

Live cloud end-to-end flows were not exercised.

## How to Test

1. Open a sandbox with cached or recorded messages and make its live session/default-chat/peer-chat subscription fail. Confirm messages and the cache remain intact, the recorded API refresh continues, and the existing live Retry action remains available.
2. Let the recorded refresh succeed, then recover the live subscription and invoke Retry. Confirm the same chat promotes successfully without dropping the draft.
3. Repeat with a root-session NotFound response. Existing recorded messages must remain readable; a successful empty recorded result must still allow lazy session initialization. An unavailable API or a truncated replay missing the requested root must not be mistaken for an empty conversation, including when the replay contains a different session.
4. Check a new session, an empty but successfully hydrated chat, and a transcript containing a failed turn. All must still load normally. Close a chat while a missing-root result is waiting for recorded history and confirm its pending work is cancelled and released.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a cloud sandbox with cached or recorded history while live Agent Host hydration succeeds or fails
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Recorded history loading and live provider hydration start concurrently; the first authoritative source completes the open. On a successful live hydration, history is cancelled off the critical path. On a failed live hydration, the changed code keeps recorded history as the authoritative source rather than accepting the failure transcript.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and replay the task's persisted AHP event history
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight fetch per task after CloudSandboxHistoryCache coalescing; cached history may provide an immediate preview while the single fresh fetch continues.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The fetch already ran in parallel, but a failed live snapshot could be accepted as live, cancel the fetch, and invalidate its cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold opens can wait for this fetch; warm opens can render the cached snapshot first. After a live failure, the request remains relevant and can complete the open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to Agent Host session state and then the selected default or peer chat state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared session subscription plus one selected chat subscription per backend session/chat; existing subscription maps reuse successful subscriptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscriptions were attempted, but their failure was rendered into a session that the sandbox facade treated as a successful live snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Live promotion waits for subscription hydration; failure now causes that candidate session to be rejected and disposed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously opened sandbox resources and transcript event/turn count; effective network cardinality is one history fetch per task, not one per reader or turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One live attempt per sandbox entry and one recorded-history attempt run concurrently. Duplicate readers share the entry; history fetches are additionally coalesced per task. Retries are serialized by liveRequested/historyRequested guards.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A positive cached transcript can render immediately while one fresh request runs. Empty/missing cache results do not masquerade as positive history. The change preserves cache and pending refresh on rejected live hydration; successful live promotion retains existing invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call flow, request guards, cache coalescing, and disposal are explicit in the inspected implementation and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent Host subscription and history endpoint durations vary by connectivity and transcript size, but the diff does not add calls or increase their effective cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes erroneous cache invalidation/cancellation on failed live hydration and adds only constant-size metadata and disposal tracking.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a missing root sandbox session and decide whether it can be initialized lazily
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the live session subscription returns NotFound, the changed code waits for the already-running recorded-history result before allowing lazy initialization. A cached accepted history resolves this immediately; a cold result can place the history request on the open critical path. The live attempt remains bounded by its existing 30-second cancellation timer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attempt Agent Host session subscription, which reports NotFound
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One live attempt for the sandbox entry, with duplicate opens sharing the entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscription ran, but its NotFound result could be accepted immediately as an empty live session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The NotFound result no longer completes the open by itself; it gates on recorded history to avoid overwriting a preserved conversation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch persisted task history to prove that no conversation exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced request per task, with a warm positive cache delivered before the fresh response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The request ran concurrently but could be cancelled when the failed live result was accepted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff moves this already-running request onto the critical path only for a root NotFound result that might otherwise erase recorded history.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One decision per opened root sandbox; history parsing scales with the task event stream, while network cardinality remains one per task.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The live NotFound attempt and recorded read start concurrently. The new await joins the existing recorded read rather than starting another request; retries remain guarded and the pending live session is disposed on failure/cancellation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm valid cached history settles the entry before the NotFound decision. Cold, empty, failed, and truncated outcomes remain distinct; failed/truncated reads do not authorize initialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new await, cache states, coalescing, cancellation, and timeout are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A cold history request can noticeably delay this rare recovery path, but duration depends on network conditions. There is no compatible cheaper authoritative source shown in the repository, and the wait is required by the change's preservation semantics.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This is an intentional correctness validation on a narrow failure path, reuses an in-flight coalesced request, and has no bounded alternative that preserves the required authority check.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close or cancel a sandbox while failed live hydration is waiting for recorded history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cancellation disposes the sandbox entry, cancels both the recorded read waiter and live token, and clears the pending live session/subscriptions; this cleanup is off the success critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel the outstanding task-history waiter and, when it is the final waiter, its shared request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One waiter release; underlying request cancellation occurs only when no task waiters remain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Entry disposal already cancelled history; the diff avoids prematurely cancelling it merely because live hydration failed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Does not block closure; cancellation propagates through tokens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose failed Agent Host session/chat subscription references
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the shared session/default-chat references and one peer-chat reference for the failed candidate; shared subscriptions remain while sibling holds exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: When failure occurred before chat URI resolution, the disposal callback skipped subscription release and could retain the failed subscription ownership.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous map/ref cleanup during disposal, with no new remote request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of concurrently active sibling chats for the same backend session; cleanup checks existing holds and releases a constant number of owned subscriptions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cleanup is token-driven and idempotent through disposable stores. A per-session hydration count prevents one failed candidate from tearing down a sibling's shared subscription.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cancellation releases only this reader. Shared cache work survives while another waiter remains; no negative failure result is pinned.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership and disposal paths are explicit and covered by the added cancellation assertions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously open sibling chats is product-dependent, but the changed cleanup reduces rather than increases retained resources.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The added pending-session owner and unconditional release call close prior cleanup gaps without introducing repeated remote work or unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load a truncated recorded replay whose requested root session is absent or present
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing history network request and replay complete before the read-only handler validates whether the requested session is represented. The changed predicate rejects an absent requested root but continues to render an included partial transcript.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the task event replay used by the validation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced fetch per task, unchanged by the predicate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same replay was fetched, but a truncated response lacking the requested root could be treated as an empty conversation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The validation runs after the existing fetch; it adds no boundary call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Predicate cost is constant after the existing session lookup; replay/folding remains proportional to event and transcript size as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged; cache coalescing and the session entry guards control parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Truncated histories are not committed to the persistent in-memory history cache. The changed validation does not alter that policy.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line and transitive fetch/cache code are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed predicate; it adds only boolean checks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the changed predicate adds no I/O, fan-out, retention, or meaningful CPU work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced live Agent Host subscription hydration, recorded-history HTTP fetch/replay, cache coalescing/invalidation, missing-root validation, truncated replay handling, retries, cancellation, and subscription/session disposal. No high-confidence actionable performance issue was introduced.
